ingredients.name: Cold unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: cut into small cubes; must be very cold for a flaky short-crust pastry

ingredients.name: Ice-cold water
ingredients.notes: about 3-4 tablespoons; added gradually until the dough just comes together

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.notes: beaten, for the egg wash to glaze the patties before baking

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken breast or thigh
ingredients.notes: cooked and very finely shredded or minced

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: freshly ground -- the dominant spice in the filling

steps.instruction: Make the pastry: sift flour and salt into a bowl. Add the cold butter cubes and rub in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs -- work quickly to keep the butter cold. Add ice water one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overwork. Wrap in cling film and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Make the filling: heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté the onion, garlic, ginger, and green chillies for 3-4 minutes until soft. Add the curry leaves, black pepper, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute.

Add the finely shredded cooked chicken. Mix well with the spiced onion base. Cook for 2-3 minutes until everything is combined and any excess moisture has evaporated -- the filling must be dry, not wet. Add lime juice, taste, and adjust seasoning. Cool completely.
Preheat the oven to 200C (400F). On a lightly floured surface, roll the chilled pastry to about 3mm thickness. Cut out circles about 12cm in diameter using a pastry cutter or upturned bowl.

Place a heaped tablespoon of the cooled filling on one half of each pastry circle. Dampen the edges with a little water. Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling to form a half-moon shape. Press the edges firmly together, then crimp with a fork.
Place on a greased baking tray. Brush the tops with beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Bake at 200C for 20-25 minutes until golden brown. Serve warm or at room temperature. Chicken patties keep well for 2 days at room temperature or 3-4 days refrigerated.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, theflavorbender.com, ralahami.com, srilankanrecipes.info, berrychik.com, and lakpura.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; strong agreement on the short-crust pastry base, the pepper-forward spiced chicken filling, and the bake (not fry) cooking method
notes: Sri Lankan chicken patties are classified as 'short eats' alongside fish cutlets (sl_049), fish rolls (sl_072), and ulundu vadai (sl_048). Unlike the other short eats in this collection which are deep-fried, chicken patties are baked -- a British colonial influence visible in both the short-crust pastry technique and the half-moon shape. They are served at virtually every Sri Lankan birthday party, high tea, and family gathering. The filling is pepper-forward rather than chilli-forward, distinguishing it from most Sri Lankan meat dishes. A fried version using oil pastry (similar to the Indian samosa technique) is a popular street-food variant but less common at home; this entry reflects the standard baked version. Other popular fillings include beef, fish (using the same filling as sl_049 fish cutlets), and vegetable.
